messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: P1 - TP job hang + CUDA OOMs on prod-gpu-cluster-7 (nccl collectives failing). Alerts firing: 3 jobs, 4 nodes. Paging oncall_sre and runtime-agent. Link: https://redwood.infra/alerts/1830015555

oncall_sre: I'm on it. Which stacks are affected? any customer-facing jobs?

maria: seeing repeated logs from tp-world 12: `NCCL WARN Timeout, rank 0 -> 3` and then `CUDA error: out of memory` in container model-serving-rls-9. GPU mem usage spikes to 100% then driver resets.

deepak: adding logs from node gpu-7b-prod: ```
[2023-11-02T03:41:10Z] ncclNet: call to connect failed: -1
[2023-11-02T03:41:12Z] NCCL WARN Allreduce timed out after 120s
[2023-11-02T03:41:13Z] libcudart: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
[2023-11-02T03:41:14Z] GPU 0: processes: model-server pid=2211 mem=24.1GB
```

oncall_sre: thanks. Customer-impact?

customer-success: AcmePay noticed increased latency on chat completions and some 500s. They're on Dedicated reserved pool with 3 reserved GPUs - their job id: apay-7743. They've flagged degraded requests since 03:40 UTC.

runtime-agent: Observed pattern: multi-GPU TP jobs with sequence length > 2048 show sustained KV-cache growth and occasional memory leak in custom quantized kernel (v1.4.2). When one rank OOMs, NCCL peers block -> hang. Kernel version: 535.86.11, cuDNN 8.4.

maria: I can reproduce on staging with a smaller replicate: start a TP job with long seqs, force a memory spike and we see the same `nccl comm timeout -> GPU reset` sequence.

oncall_sre: immediate mitigation options?

deepak: 1) Scale down TP world-size for active jobs (reduce from 8->4) to avoid cross-node collectives. 2) For reserved customer pools, fail fast to single-GPU fallback model variant. 3) Drain nodes with repeated driver resets to remove them from scheduling.

oncall_sre: do we have a single-GPU variant ready for autopilot fallback? deploy-bot, status?

deploy-bot: Canary model variant `rls-single-small-v2` is deployed in us-west and can be toggled via route rule `fallback:single_gpu` in config service. Use `redwoodctl routes set apay-7743 --policy fallback:single_gpu --dry-run` then remove dry-run when ready.

oncall_sre: okay, I'll coordinate fallback for AcmePay. Maria, can you reduce world-size on apay-7743 now?

maria: applying patch to job spec: `tensor_parallel.world_size=4` for apay-7743. Patching via `kubectl patch job apay-7743 -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"model","env":[{"name":"TP_WORLD","value":"4"}]}]}}}}'`

deepak: also enabling aggressive KV-cache eviction on those pods: set `KV_CACHE_MAX_TOKENS=1024`.

oncall_sre: I'm draining node gpu-7b-prod (cordon + drain) to stop noisy resets. `kubectl cordon gpu-7b-prod && kubectl drain gpu-7b-prod --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` executed.

maria: apay-7743 responded to TP change, started reconciling. Logs show fewer NCCL timeouts but still occasional CUDA errors on node gpu-9a-prod.

runtime-agent: Noted that driver logs on gpu-9a-prod have `Xid 79: GPU hang`. NVML reports ECC errors count incrementing on GPU1. This suggests hardware flakiness causing memory corruption leading to CUDA illegal addresses.

oncall_sre: ops_lead, should we evacuate the whole rack?

ops_lead: yes, if ECC counters increasing, mark the node for maintenance. We'll replace the GPU, but for immediate customer safety, move workloads off affected rack and enable fallback.

customer-success: AcmePay reporting errors reduced after fallback switch, but a minority of requests still see higher latency due to single-GPU throughput limits. They're happy with failover but asked for ETA on fix.

deepak: For longer-term fix: rollback quantized kernel v1.4.2 -> v1.4.1 on affected runtime image, plus restrict kernel to non-TensorParallel paths until we validate leak fix. Also add a guard to proactively OOM-kill processes that exceed mem threshold instead of letting NCCL hang.

oncall_sre: steps taken summary for handoff: 1) cordoned and drained gpu-7b-prod, 9a-prod flagged for maintenance. 2) patched apay-7743 to TP_WORLD=4 and KV_CACHE_MAX_TOKENS=1024. 3) toggled route rule to fallback single-GPU variant (deploy-bot dry-run -> executed). 4) scaled replica counts down for other TP jobs with long sequence patterns. 5) raised hardware ticket for ECC/driver investigation (ticket #HW-8721).

maria: logs attached from latest pod after changes: ```
[2023-11-02T04:05:12Z] Model step 502: forward ok
[2023-11-02T04:05:14Z] NCCL INFO Allreduce succeeded rank0->rank1
[2023-11-02T04:05:18Z] CUDA warn: OOM avoided via kv-evict
```

oncall_sre: I'm handing off to deepak and runtime-agent for root cause and remediation. Next oncall shift: @deepak will own remediation until resolved, please keep ops_lead and customer-success looped. Handoff notes: last_message_ts=1830017890.

deepak: I'll lead root cause. Immediate next steps: recreate failing job on isolated test rack with same driver/kernel and run valgrind-style memory checks, revert kernel to 1.4.1 in canary image, add process-level mem guard. ETA for code patch + canary: 6-8 hours. Hardware replacement ETA: 3-6 hours for rack dispatch.

runtime-agent: also adding new alert rule to detect repeated `Xid 79` + ECC increment to auto-silence TP jobs and trigger node evacuation to reduce noisy neighbor blast radius.

oncall_sre: customer-impact escalation: logged into incident bridge, notified AcmePay CS lead, created postmortem draft skeleton in docs: https://redwood.infra/incidents/1830015555/postmortem-draft

customer-success: AcmePay acknowledged the mitigation. They want an RCA within 48 hours and timeline for hardware fix. I'll coordinate updates.

ops_lead: marking nodes gpu-7b-prod and gpu-9a-prod as `needs-maint` in inventory. Hardware ticket updated with ECC counts and driver logs.

oncall_sre: closing pager for now; monitoring for 2 hours. If any NCCL timeouts reappear, escalate to P1. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: NOTE: This thread was created by auto-pager. Please update incident status in Ops board and attach logs to ticket HW-8721.

deepak: adding final note for handoff doc: suspected root cause = interplay of a memory leak in quantized kernel v1.4.2 + hardware ECC-induced memory corruption causing CUDA illegal accesses -> NCCL timeouts and hangs. Mitigations: driver/node isolation, TP world-size reduction, fallback to non-TP model, kernel rollback.

oncall_sre: handoff complete. Deepak and runtime-agent own next steps. I'll re-open if customer impact spikes.

customer-success: copying AcmePay contact email to ticket and posting interim update: "We've mitigated the impact by failing over to single-GPU model variant. We're investigating root cause and will provide an RCA within 48 hours."

ops_lead: scheduled maintenance window for gpu-9a-prod: 04:30-05:30 UTC. Will replace GPU and run burn-in tests.

runtime-agent: incrementing incident severity to SEV-2 in tracking doc while hardware replacement in progress.

oncall_sre: ack. logging out.
